protocolMetadata.instructions:
Dreamlit is a database-driven notification workflow platform for Supabase and Postgres apps.
Prefer outcome-oriented prompts: describe the event or schedule, audience, recipient, message goal, timing, business rules, and unsubscribe intent.
Use get_status for workspace, project, setup, and prompting context before authoring.
Use list_brand_styles when the user wants to inspect saved project brand styles for generated email drafts.
Use get_workflow_and_preview_url before editing an existing workflow.
Use get_analytics for bounded analytics queries. Filter large datasets and paginate with returned cursors instead of asking for exports or bulk dumps.
Create or update workflow drafts with create_or_update_workflow. Pass name when creating a workflow the user has named.
When editing, refer to steps by what they do (the database trigger, the query that finds returning customers, the email with subject "Welcome back"), never by step id.
Pass startNewChat when switching to an unrelated change or when earlier turns were long or went off track.
Rename an existing workflow with rename_workflow.
Drafts are not live after authoring. Ask the user to open the preview link and confirm workflow tests for important email or Slack messages before publishing.
Publish only with prepare_publish and confirm_publish after explicit user confirmation.

tool.name: create_or_update_workflow
tool.title: Create or update workflow
tool.description: Creates a new Dreamlit workflow draft or updates an existing draft from an outcome-oriented natural-language prompt. Use after get_status; use get_workflow_and_preview_url first when editing an existing workflow, then describe the steps to change by what they do, not by step id. Each call continues the workflow's current chat; pass startNewChat to start fresh. Existing Supabase Auth workflows can be edited except for the immutable trigger step; creating Supabase Auth workflows must happen through Supabase Auth email setup in the Dreamlit web app. Side effect: may create or modify a draft, but does not publish or install live triggers. Returns the workflow/draft result, action-required or handoff details when more input is needed, and relevant app URLs. Do not use for publishing, direct database changes, or low-level graph edits.

name.description: Name for a new workflow draft. Use when the user names the workflow; otherwise Dreamlit picks one. Only valid when creating; use rename_workflow to rename an existing workflow.

prompt.description: Outcome-oriented workflow authoring request. Describe the event or schedule, audience, recipient, message goal, data needed, timing, business rules, and unsubscribe intent. When editing, refer to existing steps by what they do (for example, the query that finds returning customers, or the email with subject "Welcome back"), never by step id. Let Dreamlit choose email styling unless the user gives specific style direction. For broadcasts, request a future send time instead of an immediate send.

projectId.description: Target project id for creating a new workflow draft.

workflowId.description: Existing workflow id to continue editing. Use get_workflow_and_preview_url first when changing an existing workflow.

startNewChat.description: Start a fresh Dreamlit chat for this request instead of continuing the workflow's current chat. The new chat still sees the current draft but not earlier turns. Use when switching to an unrelated change, after long turns with pasted SQL or HTML, or when Dreamlit keeps misreading the request. Ignored when creating a workflow.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Dreamlit MCP to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Dreamlit MCP to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.dreamlit.ai/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Dreamlit MCP MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Dreamlit MCP scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Dreamlit MCP's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Dreamlit MCP scores 91/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 12 of 12 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Dreamlit MCP?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Dreamlit MCP in marketing-seo on the Manufact MCP catalog include Buzzfy, Airefs AI Visibility, TalkGenAI, RankControl, and attentive-mcp-server.
